how.title: How uFeed works
how.lead: Choose topics to keep, blacklist words or phrases, or use both. This free browser extension gently blurs matching posts; every post stays right where it is.
steps: Choose what to keep or block

Open the uFeed popup and choose what to filter. For topic filtering, write one subject per line as a short phrase of two to five words. Use words people use in posts—for example, “software engineering” instead of “tech.” Skip full sentences; commas are optional. Or use the keyword blacklist on its own to blur posts containing the words or phrases you list.

On X, LinkedIn, or Reddit, uFeed checks each post against your topics or blacklist. Topic checks happen in your browser; blacklist matches are checked directly against the words and phrases you listed.
See more or less of what you want

When you use topics, posts outside them are gently blurred. A blacklist also blurs posts with matching words or phrases, even when they fit your topics. With only a blacklist, unmatched posts stay visible. Tap a blurred post—or focus it and press Enter—to see it whenever you want.
Adjust strictness and peek at close calls. Rate posts to help uFeed learn what you want to see more or less of; ratings stay on your device.
details: 🔒 Made to feel simple and stay private

There is no sign-up, account, or uFeed server. The model is downloaded once and cached by your browser. Your topics and the posts you read are not sent to us. uFeed is free and open source, so you can look through the project yourself.
🌍 Choose the language that suits you

The default model works in English. If your feeds are in other languages, you can choose the optional multilingual model in the popup. It needs a larger one-time download; your topics and settings stay the same.
A helpful nudge, not a perfect judge

uFeed recognises subjects, not quality. It can blur something you would have liked, or leave something you would rather skip. You are always one click away from the full feed, and if uFeed stops working, posts remain visible.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: The extension keeps feed text and settings on your device. On a first install in Chrome or Firefox, your browser opens a page on ufeed.es; the site host receives a normal page request.
sections: What uFeed reads

On X (x.com and twitter.com), LinkedIn and Reddit, uFeed reads the text of posts in the page to compare them with your topics. The comparison happens in your browser. Post text is held in memory while it is scored, then discarded. It is not written to disk, sent over the network or logged. uFeed does nothing on other websites.
What stays on your device

Your topics and settings are saved in your browser’s local extension storage. If you turn on “Learn from my thumbs,” uFeed also saves number-based representations of posts you rate. These can retain some information about the original post, so they are treated as personal data. They stay on your device, with up to 50 positive and 50 negative ratings per topic.

If you choose to export a backup, the file contains your settings and any saved ratings. Keep that file somewhere private. Importing a backup replaces the settings and ratings already in the extension.
What uFeed sends

On a first install in Chrome or Firefox, uFeed opens its welcome page at ufeed.es. Your browser makes a normal page request, which reveals your IP address, standard request details and the selected language path to the site host. It contains no feed text, topics or extension settings. Separately, the first time a language model is needed, your browser downloads it from Hugging Face. That request reveals your IP address and the requested model to that service. Your browser caches the model for later use. Neither request includes feed content or settings.
Permissions

Supported websites: to read post text and apply the blur on X, LinkedIn and Reddit.
Storage: to keep your settings and optional ratings on your device.
Offscreen page (Chrome): to run the multilingual model in a shared extension worker. It receives text for scoring but cannot read the website.
Deleting your data

Use “Clear tuning” to delete ratings, or “Reset” to clear ratings and restore default settings. Uninstalling uFeed removes its locally stored data. Nothing is held by us, and there is no account to delete.
Children and changes
uFeed is not directed at children and collects no data from anyone. If this policy changes, this page’s date will be updated.

sections: Use and limitations

uFeed is provided “as is,” without warranties of any kind, to the fullest extent permitted by law. It uses a statistical model and can blur posts you wanted to see or leave visible posts you did not. Do not rely on it where missing a post could matter. We do not promise that it will always be available or keep working when social websites change.
Liability

To the fullest extent allowed by law, the uFeed contributors are not liable for indirect or consequential loss arising from use of the software, including content you missed because it was blurred. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited.
Social websites

uFeed changes how X, LinkedIn and Reddit pages appear in your own browser. It is independent of those services and is not endorsed by them. Their names belong to their respective owners. Your use of each service remains subject to its own terms, and changes to a service may affect how uFeed works.
Your data
uFeed processes feed text on your device and sends no feed content or settings to us.
Changes
These terms may be updated; the date above will change when they are. Continued use after an update means you accept the updated terms.
